task.title: Expose finite recurrence inventory through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/867 by rendering the kernel recurrence inventory as deterministic compact JSON from a read-only developer command.
acceptance_criteria: Provide recurrence inspect over one caller-selected existing database without creating or mutating it.
Emit complete recurrence fields in deterministic identifier order, including an empty array for an empty valid store.
Fail non-zero with one escaped diagnostic and no partial stdout for missing, unreadable, or corrupted storage.

attempts.diagnostic: Three focused CLI integration tests failed because recurrence was not a recognized command.
attempts.patch: Added success, empty-inventory, missing-storage, corruption, ordering, and non-mutation command coverage.

attempts.summary: Implemented a minimal read-only inventory adapter.
attempts.diagnostic: The kernel already owned discovery and validation, so the CLI only needed argument dispatch, deterministic serialization, and stable diagnostics.
attempts.patch: Added recurrence inspect over RecurrenceStore::open_read_only and list, compact response types, categorized failures, help text, and ADR-0041.

attempts.summary: Waited for genuine review capacity before merge.
attempts.diagnostic: CodeRabbit initially returned Review limit reached, making its green status a false green.
attempts.patch: Preserved exact head efa96add with auto-merge disabled, resumed once after cooldown and budget checks, and merged after CodeRabbit's recent-review summary covered the complete base-to-head range with no actionable comments.

outcome.summary: Operators can inspect the complete finite recurrence inventory as deterministic JSON without granting the CLI write or execution authority.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0167-recurrence-inventory-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 171 records: 171 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: Keep validation and ordering in the kernel and make the CLI a thin serialization boundary.
Fail before stdout so consumers never mistake partial inventory for authoritative state.
An inspection command should preserve missing storage rather than initialize it.
Review cooldowns are merge blockers, not timing hints to ignore.
